## 1. What this application is

`u2giants/shared-db` is the canonical repo for **one** Supabase PostgreSQL database shared by five applications:

| App | What it is | Repo |
|---|---|---|
| PopDAM | digital asset management | `u2giants/popdam3` |
| PopCRM | customer relationship management | `u2giants/popcrm-web` |
| DesignFlow PLM ("dflow") | product lifecycle management | `popcre/designflow-*` (six repos) |
| PopPIM | product information management | `u2giants/poppim-web` |
| monitor | Synology NAS monitoring | `u2giants/synology-monitor` |

Schema is authored here, proved on **preview** (`rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`), promoted to **production** (`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`). **One bad migration breaks all five.**

**Who works here:** AI sessions, 3–7 at once, sometimes in the same working copy. The owner, **Albert Hazan**, is a business owner and **not a programmer**. **Controls must be mechanical; a rule that needs a human to remember it does not happen here.** That premise drives everything below.

**Branch model:** branch + PR, and **the AI merges its own PRs**. The repo is **PUBLIC**.

## 4. Everything we tried that did NOT work

1. **My scrub tool was ceremony.** It proposed redactions, Albert would approve them, and the migration script pasted every block **verbatim** — nothing consumed the report. Kimi ranked it BLOCKING and was right. Fixed with a redaction map that `--create` refuses to run without.
2. **Retiring the queue would have deleted ten live safety rules.** `AGENTS.md` pointed at the file for the standing facts, including the **background-task-chip ban**. Kimi caught it. Now `AGENTS.md` §12.
3. **The pointer guard could be switched off by the same PR that regrew the queue.** `POINTER_MODE` lived in the repo it guarded. **A control the guarded thing can switch off is not a control.** Grok caught it; the flag is deleted.
4. **The guard missed the exact shape it exists to catch.** It knew section titles but not `### REQUEST — …`, which is what a stale machine actually appends. Grok caught it.
5. **I wrote a literal NUL byte into the scrub tool.** Kimi caught it and refused to verify that file until it was gone. Ran fine; corrupted every diff.
6. **My idempotency check duplicated on two paths** — close an issue and a re-run recreates it; rename a title and it makes a second. Now the `(WI-nn)` body marker over `--state all`.
7. **I proposed classifying the 33 orphan migrations by object existence.** Dangerous: a migration whose job was to **DROP** something looks identical to one never applied. Kimi caught it before it reached execution.
8. **My new plan said "open an issue per backlog item". Eight already had issues.** Would have created eight duplicates while claiming to reduce sprawl.
9. **Both review wrappers aborted on a clean tree.** `ai-kimi` refuses if the tree changed during a review — it was **my own edit** mid-run. **Do not touch the tree while a review runs.**
10. **Kimi's first round on the new plan couldn't read it** — I left it on an unmerged branch. Cost a round.
11. **The rename erased "coordinator" from the skill triggers**, which would have broken the phrasing every existing issue uses. Restored as synonyms.

## 5. Root causes and key findings

**A. Nothing checked a skill against the rulebook it summarises.** `shared-db-change` said *"DDL via MCP `apply_migration` only"* while `AGENTS.md` §12 fact 6 says that MCP **may be bound to PRODUCTION with no way to aim it at preview**. A session following it could have applied DDL to production believing it was safe. It drifted for weeks; **three model reviews missed it** because the skills live in `u2giants/ai-devops` and no CI run sees both repos. Now `scripts/check-skill-drift.mjs`, wired into the offline test lane. **It found three more real drifts on its first run.**

**B. The production lane is built and never exercised — not broken.** I first said "281 runs, 0 successes, never worked". **Wrong.** `production-dry-run` only runs on `workflow_dispatch` with `target=production`; the 142 skips are pull requests behaving correctly. It is deliberately dry-run-only (`Refuse production apply` is step 1) and well-built: exact-SHA confirmation, typed confirmation, `production` environment, bounded allowlist via `scripts/production_migration_guard.py`. **Kimi verified in code that the guard deletes anything outside the allowlist and `verify-dry-run` demands an exact match — so the 33 orphans cannot ride along.** ⚠️ The verifier is coupled to CLI **output wording** (`:417`); a Supabase upgrade breaks it in a way that looks like a migration fault.

**C. A written rule does not reach a session already running.** Albert's ruling landed ~17:00. At 22:26 a live session filed #578 asking for the git-history scrub that ruling had **cancelled**. I predicted this failure and wrote the ruling at the top of §6.7 to stop it. **It happened anyway.** This is plan item C.

**D. Losing "what is next" was a real regression.** The old file had a top; 71 issues do not. Plan item D — but the recommendation is to build **nothing** and let `gh issue list --label now` be the board, because a rendered copy of a query is a stale cache.

**E. `AGENTS.md:1130-1136` is stale** and reads as "the migrations lane cannot be hardened" — discouraging exactly the fix item A needs. Settled by Kimi against the code. Plan item F.

**F. Asking a second reviewer "what did the first miss" beats asking "review this".** Grok found three blocking defects in work Kimi had already passed, specifically because it was told so.

## 7. Constraints and gotchas in force

1. **Branch + PR; you merge it yourself.** Never commit to `main`.
2. **Commit identity `Albert Hazan <u2giants@users.noreply.github.com>`** — check `git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT` before the first commit.
3. **`main` moves constantly** — several other sessions are active. Expect `gh pr update-branch`; it happened five times today. `strict: true` means a behind branch cannot merge.
4. **The Supabase MCP is bound to PRODUCTION and takes no project parameter.** Call `get_project_url` first, every time. Read-only measurement is fine; writes are not.
5. **Never `--include-all` against production.** It would sweep in all 33 unrecorded migrations.
6. **Every count in the plan and in this file was measured 2026-08-07. Re-derive; do not quote.**
7. **Marker #587 is open and is not yours.**
8. **Do not touch the working tree while `ai-kimi` or `ai-grok-review` is running** — both abort on a changed tree, and it is usually your own edit.
9. **`.ai/reviews/` is deliberately tracked** (14 files). Both wrappers advise gitignoring it. **That advice is wrong here** — Kimi conceded the point.
10. **Windows line endings:** `.mjs`/`.md` edits warn `LF will be replaced by CRLF`. Harmless; do not "fix" it.
11. **`verify` is not a required check** but it now passes — nanoid was fixed (#573). If it goes red again, fix it; a permanently red check is one nobody reads.
12. **Do not rewrite git history** for the Disney data. Cancelled by ruling.
